ambiguities_or_notes: Every source block (25) has a matching target block, with page markers, numbering, quotation structure, and italics preserved.

Website Circle of Reading paragraphs served as the first draft; each was re-read against the Russian and revised where it drifted (omissions, additions, generic he/his, terminology, attribution form); blocks 2, 3, 4 had no website counterpart and were translated fresh.

The three opening sentences had no website counterpart and were translated fresh, keeping Tolstoy's italics on «всё» (vsyo, 'everything'), «что должно» (chto dolzhno, 'what ought'), «нужное» (nuzhnoe, 'needed'), and «приятное» (priyatnoe, 'pleasant'). «Нужный» (nuzhnyy) is 'needed' throughout reading 2, «зло» (zlo) is 'evil' (not 'harm'), and «дерзость» (derzost') is 'insolence'; Kant's «козел» (kozyol) is a 'he-goat', which the proverb requires.
